title: Single-root fan-out conditions
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $G$ and $E$ be finite gate lists, and let $r$ be a natural number. The single-root fan-out conditions require that every old vertex $v$ with $n\le v<n+|G|$ has fan-out zero in $E$, and every vertex $v\ge n$ has fan-out at most one in $E$. If $r\ge n$, then $r$ has fan-out zero; moreover, either $r<n$ or $r\ge n+|G|$. Every vertex $v$ with $n+|G|\le v<n+|G|+|E|$ other than $r$ has fan-out exactly one in $E$.

old vertices in [n,n+|G|) have fan-out zero in E
every vertex at least n has fan-out at most one in E
if r is at least n then its fan-out is zero

new vertices in [n+|G|, n+|G|+|E|) other than r have fan-out one
